subject: SLA template: regional maintenance carve-outs & monthly remedy scaling (CloudHarbor)
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cloudharbor.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.com
Cc: Emma Li <emma@cloudharbor.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Initial: SLA template questions and regional maintenance carve-outs

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for sending the updated SLA. We reviewed the document with our legal and infra teams and have two main concerns we want to flag before we proceed:

1) Regional maintenance carve-outs: the proposed wording allows for maintenance windows to be scheduled by region without a notification lead longer than 72 hours. For our EU production, we need a min notice of 7 days for any maintenance that may affect availability above 1%.

2) Monthly remedy scaling: the credit ladder in section 4.2 looks pro-rata but doesn't factor in sustained degraded latency across multiple short incidents. We need a model that aggregates short degradations so remediation isn’t diluted.

I've attached a suggested redline and a CSV with our preferred maintenance calendar (internal reference). Can we align on these items and propose a mutual action plan?

Proposed next step: can Laura or someone on your contracts team confirm what flexibility you have for 7-day notice and an aggregated remedy calculation?

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds
VP of Infrastructure
CloudHarbor

Attachments: SLA_Template_CloudHarbor_v3.pdf (pdf, 76KB), maintenance_windows_proposal.csv (csv, 3KB)

From: lukas_meyer@redwood.com <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cloudharbor.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Dec 2025 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Initial: SLA template questions and regional maintenance carve-outs

Tom — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. Looping in Laura and Marissa to confirm the contract-side constraints and the remedy math.

Quick answers up front:
- Notice: we can commit to 7 days notice for any maintenance that is expected to impact an EU region's availability by >1% (agreeing to your ask makes sense). For high-severity emergency maintenance we still need emergency carveouts; we propose an emergency protocol with a post-event review and root-cause disposition.
- Remedy aggregation: Marissa, our pricing/ops lead, has a draft aggregation model that pools short-duration latency degradations over the monthly window and calculates credits using a weighted-resolve formula. It keeps per-event caps but prevents dilution — attaching summary below.

Next steps: Laura — could you confirm whether we need a formal SOW amendment or if this can be captured in the SLA appendix? If we can get sign-off on the 7-day notice commitment and the aggregation approach, I'll push an updated SLA PDF.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
lukas_meyer@redwood.com
O: +1 415 555 0124

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.com, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cloudharbor.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 08:47:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Initial: SLA template questions and regional maintenance carve-outs

Tom, Lukas — I reviewed the redline and Lukas's summary. We can accept the 7-day notice for non-emergency maintenance that is reasonably expected to affect EU production >1%. We will add an explicit emergency maintenance carveout with:

- Definition of "emergency maintenance" (security incident, critical vulnerability, imminent data loss)
- Requirement for an after-action report within 72 hours and follow-up remediation timeline
- Commitment to minimize customer impact and to use lowest-impact windows when feasible

About the remedy aggregation:
- We will include the aggregation methodology as an appendix (not requiring a separate SOW) so it travels with the SLA.
- Cap behavior: monthly credit cap will remain, but the ladder will apply to the aggregated monthly metric rather than per isolated short blips. That prevents the dilution you called out while keeping a hard monthly cap.

Tom — can you confirm CloudHarbor is comfortable with an appendix approach (rather than SOW)? If yes, I'll circulate a tracked PDF with the specific appendix language and the 7-day notice clause.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Contract Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_appendix_draft.txt (plain text, 2KB)

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cloudharbor.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, lukas_meyer@redwood.com
Cc: Emma Li <emma@cloudharbor.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2025 16:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Initial: SLA template questions and regional maintenance carve-outs

Laura, Lukas — thanks, that's helpful. CloudHarbor is comfortable with the appendix approach. A few small asks before we finalize:

1) Add a minimum of two scheduled maintenance blackout windows per quarter where Redwood agrees not to perform non-emergency changes that could affect EU production metrics unless mutually agreed. We use these windows for major releases and coordination.
2) In the appendix aggregation formula, please add an explicit example calculation showing two short latency blips (2m @1.8x P95, 7m @2.1x P95) aggregated into the monthly metric so our ops team can validate.

If you can send a tracked version with those two additions, we should be ready to sign. Happy to do a 20-minute call if easier.

Tom Reynolds
VP of Infrastructure
CloudHarbor
